findings.evidence: `<meta charset="utf-8">` is the only meta tag present; no `<meta name="viewport" ...>` is included
findings.fix: Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` to the head.
findings.violation: Without a viewport meta tag, this workspace UI mockup will render at desktop scale on mobile browsers, defeating the purpose of a UI mockup meant to be viewed/tested across devices.

findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced last week." followed by a `<ul>` with only three `<li>` entries (Holiday Campaign Assets, Support Backlog Triage, Mobile App Revamp)
findings.fix: Either add the missing fourth project to the list or correct the count in the paragraph to 3.
findings.violation: The stated project count (4) doesn't match the number of projects actually listed (3), an internal inconsistency.

findings.evidence: `<div id="workspace-overview-recent">` sits directly under the "Your projects" heading with no label indicating it's a partial/recent subset, despite the div's own id containing "recent"
findings.fix: Add a visible heading (e.g., "Recent projects") above the list, or rename the div if it is meant to be the full list.
findings.violation: A reader has no way to tell whether this list is meant to be the complete project list or just a "recent" subset, since no heading or caption communicates that distinction.

findings.fix: Add visible text (e.g., "Duplicate") or an icon with the aria-label retained for accessibility.
findings.violation: The button has no visible text content or icon, so sighted users have no indication of its purpose or even that it's a distinct control - only screen reader users get the aria-label.

findings.evidence: `<input id="project-settings-name-input" type="text" value="Q3 Roadmap">`, `<input id="invite-member-email-input" type="email">`, `<select id="notification-settings-digest-input">` - none have a `name` attribute
findings.fix: Add appropriate `name` attributes to each form control.
findings.violation: Without `name` attributes, these fields would not be included in form submission data if this mockup were wired to a real backend.

findings.evidence: The form has a `` and, separately, `Continue`
findings.fix: Remove the redundant control - e.g., have the Save button itself navigate to `#invite-sent` on success, and drop the separate Continue link.
findings.violation: It's unclear whether clicking "Save" or "Continue" is what actually sends the invite; having both a submit button and a separate forward-navigation link for the same form creates ambiguous, overlapping affordances.

findings.evidence: "You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list."
findings.fix: Either add an archived-projects-list section/link or remove the reference to restoring from it.
findings.violation: The mockup has no page, section, or link anywhere for an "archived projects list," so this refers to a destination that doesn't exist in the document.

findings.evidence: Both are `type="submit"` buttons inside forms with no `action` attribute and no associated confirmation section or forward link, unlike the invite flow (`#invite-sent`) and archive flow (`#project-archived`) which both lead to explicit confirmation screens
findings.fix: Add a confirmation state/section (or at least a success message) reached after saving, matching the pattern used for invites and archiving.
findings.violation: Saving project settings or notification settings has no defined outcome or user feedback in the mockup, inconsistent with the confirmation pattern used elsewhere for state-changing actions.
